jobs.description: Venice | Secure AI Agents Check out our newest report on the State of Identity in AI Venice is coming to Identiverse Check us out >> Solutions Secure AI Agents Zero Standing Privileges Just-in-Time Access Replace Your Legacy PAM Context-Aware Access Audit Sign-Off Learn Blog State of AI Report Customers About Partners get a demo get a demo it starts with identity Secure Access for AI Agents AI agents accumulate access, operate without ownership, and outrun the tools built to track them. Standalone agent security products see what the agents do, but not who sent them, what they were asked to do, or what permissions their task actually requires. Venice already holds that context. Agents are governed according to the same model as every other privileged identity, the user, the task, the scope. Your browser does not support the video tag. NEW | Runtime Identity Gateway for Agents A New Identity Type Just Showed Up For Work AI agents are created by humans, scoped by permissions, and act in real systems - that's an identity, and identity is where governance happens. Venice sits between every agent and every resource, evaluating every call against the declared task. Ephemeral by Default Agents get access for the task and access is revoked the moment the task ends. Access Only by Request Agents are forced to request access keeping them in policy and stopping lateral movement. Runtime Authorization Agents don't pause for a policy review. Venice evaluates, decides, and intervenes while the call is still happening. Agent Ownership at Creation Venice traces every agent back to the human who built it and the task it was built for. Access is granted for the task, gone when the task is done. Catch Drift in the Call Venice evaluates every agent call against the declared intended task in real time, blocks calls outside that scope, and ties every action to a named identity. Session audit for agents Venice records every request, access grant, and session action and ties them to named identities. Reports are organized for fast investigations and quick audits. jobs.description: Cookie Notices and Cookie Consent | Cookiepedia All About Cookies What are Cookies? Types of Cookies Online Tracking Technologies The Benefits of Cookies Cookies and Online Privacy How to Manage Cookies Google Chrome Firefox Firefox (iOS) Firefox (Android) Safari (Desktop) Safari (Mobile) Microsoft Edge Internet Explorer Opera New Cookie Controls for Chrome IAB Legal Text EU Cookie Directive EU Cookie Directive Cookie Laws Across Europe Cookie Law in the UK Cookie Law Compliance Guidance Cookies Consent How To Complain About Cookies The Cookiepedia Database About Cookiepedia Using Cookiepedia How We Classify Cookies Cookies and Privacy Policy Cookie Notices and Cookie Consent Explained Cookies are integral to the way modern websites work. Most personalisation and social media integration on websites relies on cookies in one way or another. However they can be used in a way that doesn’t benefit visitors, and they are often used to track people across the web, and build up profiles that are very valuable to brands and advertisers for targeted marketing. This is often seen as an invasion of privacy , and because cookies are a fairly quiet technology – this can be happening to you without you realising it, or being able to stop it if you wanted to. To help you become more aware of this activity, and give you a say in whether you want to allow it to happen, new EU-wide privacy legislation was put in place in 2011. This has become known as the Cookie Law . The Cookie Law requires that websites give you clear, detailed information about how they use cookies, and provide ways for you to signal whether or not you want to allow such use. The website is then required by law to respect your wishes. This might mean they block the cookies you don’t like, or they don’t let you access the site – however you should expect to be given the choice. Some websites will allow you to choose which types of cookies to allow or block, although in some cases if you do this you may not be able to use or see all of a website. If a website you visit is not giving you sufficient information or choice, and the company that owns it is based in the EU, then it may be breaking the law, and you can take action against the owner. This website has been created to help people understand better what cookies are and how they are used by different websites. You can use it to look up your favourite websites, and soon you will be able to search for information about specific cookies to understand what they are used for.
